new_statements.translation: Compare the verb biyeymiyán = P. āmadan 'to come': present sg. 1 miäm 2 miyey 3 miyä; pl. 1 miyeym 2 miyeyd 3 miyän; simple past sg. 1 biyämiyam 2 biyämiyey 3 biyäme; pl. 1 biyeymiyeym 2 biyeymiyeyd 3 biyeymiyan (stress on the penultimate syllable, unlike the infinitive, which sounds the same to the ear with the difference that in it the stress is on the last syllable).

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for goza1238, so there is nothing to agree with or contradict; the work adds one usable but partial datum (final stress on an infinitive vs. penultimate stress on the homophonous 3pl preterite). It is compatible with the only other stress remark held by the project for this language, Ivanow 1931 p. 362 (earlier reading): the substantive verb is 'dárä, with the accent on the first syllable', 'not dorä, as one would expect' -- again a verb-form-specific remark implying an expected (final) default that neither source states outright. new_statements.rule_in_words: No general statement of word-stress placement. The phonology section (pp. 160-161, 'توضیحاتی درباره‌ی دستگاه واجی') gives the vowel system (a, ä, e, i, o, u), the consonant inventory and six numbered consonant correspondences with Persian, and has no stress/accent paragraph. The only stress datum is incidental (p. 163): the infinitive biyeymiyán 'to come' carries stress on its final syllable (marked with an acute in the transcription), while the segmentally identical 3pl preterite biyeymiyan is stressed on the penult, so stress position distinguishes the two forms. This is a form-specific contrast (infinitive final-stressed, finite person-marked form not), not a rule for the lexicon.
new_statements.exceptions: none beyond the infinitive vs. 3pl-preterite contrast itself
new_statements.identity_note: The article treats 'گویش الموتی' (the dialect of the Alamut district, Rudbar-e Alamut, Qazvin) as a whole, citing Ivanow's Gozarkhon material and mentioning the villages Bala Ruch and Pa'in Ruch (p. 164); data mainly from manuscripts of a native speaker, Ziya'oddin Shahvarzi. It is a Persian translation (Ahmad Samiei Gilani) of Kinga Maciuszak's 1995 English article in Iran 33, so the two catalog 'works' Maciuszak 1995 and Samiei 1995 are one text in two languages.

sources.note: '1. Notes on Phonology' (pp. 357-359) covers vowels, consonants and correspondences with Literary Persian and says nothing about word stress. The only accent remark is p. 362, on the substantive verb: 'it is always pronounced not dorä, as one would expect, but as dárä, with the accent on the first syllable' (paradigm dáräm, dári, dárä; dárim, dárin, dáren) - a note on one form, not a general rule; the expected default is not stated. page scan of p. 362 viewed to confirm the acute on dárä.
